title: Stone Town Walking Tour
bestTimeToGo: Year-round, mornings are cooler and ideal for walking
highlights: Explore the UNESCO World Heritage labyrinth of Stone Town
Visit the House of Wonders and the Old Fort
Discover the historic slave market site and Anglican Cathedral
Wander through Darajani Market bursting with tropical fruit and spices
Admire intricately carved Zanzibari doors dating back centuries
includes: Hotel pickup and drop-off within Stone Town
Entrance fees to all listed sites
Fresh juice stop at a local café
excludes: Meals beyond the included juice stop

itinerary.dayBody: Your guide meets you at your hotel and leads you into the winding alleyways of Stone Town. Begin at the Old Fort and House of Wonders on the waterfront, then weave through the old quarter past the Sultan’s Palace and the Persian baths. Stop at the former slave market, now home to the Anglican Cathedral, for a moving historical account. Continue to Darajani Market where vendors sell everything from fresh tuna to jackfruit. Pause for a cold sugar-cane juice before visiting some of the town’s most famous carved doors. The tour ends back at the waterfront where you can linger at Forodhani Gardens.

whatToBring: Modest clothing that covers shoulders and knees
Small cash for souvenirs or tips
pickupInfo: Complimentary pickup from any hotel within Stone Town. For hotels outside Stone Town, pickup can be arranged for an additional fee.
cancellationPolicyShort: Free cancellation up to 24 hours before the tour.

seo.title: Stone Town Walking Tour | Zanzibar Heavenly
seo.description: Walk the UNESCO World Heritage streets of Stone Town with a local guide. Visit the House of Wonders, Darajani Market, and centuries-old carved doors on this half-day tour.

content:
Step back in time on a guided walk through Stone Town, the cultural heart of Zanzibar and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. This ancient quarter is a living tapestry of Swahili, Arab, Persian, Indian, and European influences—visible in every carved doorway, crumbling palace, and bustling market stall.

Your knowledgeable local guide will lead you through a maze of narrow alleyways where the scent of cloves and cardamom drifts from open doorways, past mosques and Hindu temples standing side by side, and into courtyards where generations of traders have done business. You will hear stories of sultans and slaves, merchants and explorers, gaining a deep understanding of the island’s layered history. The tour is designed at a relaxed pace with plenty of time for photographs, questions, and spontaneous discoveries around every corner.
